name: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
problem: Transformers spread FLOPs UNIFORMLY across all input positions and all layers, so easy tokens and hard tokens cost the same - compute is not allocated where it is needed.
mechanism: Per layer, cap the number of tokens that may participate in the self-attention and MLP computation at a fixed budget k chosen A PRIORI; a learned router selects the top-k tokens by an auxiliary predictor, and non-selected tokens' residual stream is carried forward untouched. Because k is fixed in advance the computation graph is STATIC with known tensor shapes - unlike other conditional-computation methods - so it does not break batching or kernels - while the IDENTITY of the k tokens stays fluid, making allocation dynamic and context-sensitive per token. Total compute is predictable; the distribution across time and depth is not.
speedup_reported: Models match baseline performance FOR EQUIVALENT FLOPS AND WALL-CLOCK TRAINING TIME, but require a FRACTION OF THE FLOPs PER FORWARD PASS, and can be upwards of 50% faster to step during post-training sampling. The 50%-faster figure is about the TRAINING/sampling step, not decode latency, and the FLOPs reduction is the durable result.
notes: ADOPTION: research-only. IMPORTANT CLASSIFICATION NOTE, recorded deliberately: this is categorised inference-time-compute rather than speculative-decoding because it changes WHICH tokens are computed, not how many tokens are produced per step - it is per-token adaptive depth/width, not speculation, and conflating the two would misattribute the speedup mechanism. Its static-shape property is what makes it usable at all in a serving system, and that is the single most transferable engineering fact in this record. VENUE NOTE: no venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar and the arXiv comment carries no venue, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = ArXiv v1 (Apr 2024). Note the claim is parity at equal FLOPs plus lower FLOPs per forward pass - NOT a standalone speedup over a deployed baseline, and there is no serving-system evaluation in the paper.
